findings.summary: The dock-fission/goo-split hallmark is fully designable on the EXISTING substrate with ZERO new engine — the four pieces are all on disk: (1) the ONE SpringProgress + inheriting --dock-morph-t scalar (dockMorphContext.ts / useDockOrientationMorph.ts) is the clock; (2) the CSS-SVG-goo bridge (morph-bridge.css + the feGaussianBlur stdDev=7 + feColorMatrix "0 0 0 20 -9" threshold authored in morph-showcase.vue:242-257) is the metaball substrate, Safari-safe (filter:url() works in WebKit); (3) ElementMorph + springTimingFunction (the kf rect-delta substrate useLiquidReveal/useDockCtaReceive both compose) does the per-piece FLIP to named target rects; (4) useLiquidFlex gives the volume-preserving --stretch squish off the scalar derivative. The mechanism: one control NECKS off the dock plate via a SPLIT-direction generalization of the merge-bridge — flip the existing recipe from "two plates fly TO one center and merge" (the V↔H teardrop) to "N plates fly FROM one center toward N named target rects and detach." Each piece is a REAL DOM glass element (a .glass-floating/.glass-deep disc/pill) whose transform rides its own --split-t (the per-piece position projected off the ONE spring value 0→1), and the goo bridge LAYER (the same feColorMatrix threshold, region-clipped to the union bbox for Safari budget) sits BEHIND them painting the necking metaball seam that visually fuses piece↔dock until the neck thins to nothing at ~t=0.55, after which each real piece reads as a clean detached disc. Re-merge is the same spring run backward (target 0); PRM is the pin()-precedent instant seat (no bridge paint, pieces snap to slots). The design is BE.W-DOCK-FISSION + proof:dock-fission with 6 source clauses + a Safari-region/budget π.
findings.detail:
THE MECHANISM IN FULL — useDockFission / <DockSplit>.

== A. THE TOPOLOGY GENERALIZATION (merge-to-one → detach-N) ==
The shipped morph-bridge.css (src/styles/dock/morph-bridge.css:68-149) is a 2-plate MERGE: a tall vertical plate + a wide horizontal plate, each RESERVING its full footprint (one layout solve) and NECKING its silhouette toward the shared center via clip-path: inset() on --dock-morph-t, the two fusing under the goo filter at t≈0.5. Fission INVERTS the flow + generalizes the count: instead of two fixed plates converging to one center, N pieces DIVERGE from the dock plate's edge toward N named target rects. The bridge's existing "neck travel = (reservedExtent − circleExtent)/2 · f(t)" inset math (lines 114-145) is exactly the necking primitive — fission reuses it per-seam, one seam per detaching piece, the inset GROWING (neck thinning) as the piece travels away.

== B. THE ONE-SPRING / PER-PIECE --split-t (no second engine) ==
ONE SpringProgress on DOCK_SPRING (constants.ts:75, response 0.32 / ζ 0.7) writes a single normalized 0→1 scalar `--dock-split-t` to the .glass-dock-frame root (the inheriting @property pattern, dock.css:74 — register --dock-split-t as syntax:"<number>" inherits:true initial:0 in property-regs.css, the --dock-morph-t twin). `t=0` = fully merged (dock is one pill/bar); `t=1` = fully fissioned (N detached pieces at slots). Each piece i derives its OWN position as a PURE f(--dock-split-t): the piece's transform interpolates from the dock-edge anchor (t=0) to its named target rect (t=1). This is the useDockOrientationMorph driver shape transplanted (useDockOrientationMorph.ts:128-149 writeScalar): one spring → one scalar → N pieces each reading it. CRITICAL: the per-piece --split-t is NOT N springs — it is the ONE scalar, with each piece's target-rect offset baked into its CSS interpolation (or its ElementMorph delta). Interruptible re-base on a mid-flight re-toggle is the exact ensureSpringRunning() inherited-velocity pattern (dockMorphContext.ts:255-266) — a re-merge mid-split carries velocity.

== C. THE NAMED TARGET RECTS (the slots) ==
useDockFission(dockRef, { pieces, corner? }) takes `pieces: readonly DockFissionPiece[]` where each piece = { id, slot, glyph?, content? } and `slot` resolves a TARGET RECT relative to the dock frame. The slots match the V1 silhouette (f_035/f_038/f_042): a 3-piece split = { left-circle (music-chip), center-pill (now-playing), right-circle (search) } at fixed gaps. The target rect is measured ONCE per fission episode (a getBoundingClientRect of a hidden layout-slot OR a declarative geometry off --dock-control-size + the gap token) — the FLIP measure useDockCtaReceive does (useDockCtaReceive.ts:222-232). The ElementMorph path: per piece, ElementMorph(dockEdgeAnchorRect, slotRect) driven FORWARD 0→1 by `--dock-split-t` (the useDockCtaReceive FORWARD-play, line 253-267), so each piece flies+reshapes from the dock edge onto its slot. Pieces that survive a context-silhouette change FLIP to new slots (the jubilance "CONTEXTUAL RECONFIGURE WIT", gap map L417).

== D. REAL DOM GLASS PIECES vs THE GOO BRIDGE LAYER (the two-layer model) ==
This is the load-bearing architecture split, mirroring morph-bridge.css's own header (line 16): "The bridge is DECORATIVE only … the real DOM docks crossfade UNDER it." Fission keeps that EXACT model:
 (1) THE REAL PIECES — N actual DOM elements (a <DockFissionPiece> each composing .glass-floating or the .glass-deep tier + --glass-accent for the per-piece hue, the iOS magenta-search/warm-music chips f_038). These carry the CONTENT (glyph, now-playing art, transport), are interactive/tappable, ride z-10. Their transform = the per-piece --split-t position; their opacity stays ~1 (they are the real surfaces, NOT crossfaded out).
 (2) THE GOO BRIDGE LAYER — a single .dock-fission-bridge behind the pieces (z-0), containing N+1 goo-PLATES (one warm-cream radial-gradient capsule per piece-seam + the dock-core plate), all under ONE filter:url(#dock-fission-goo) (the SAME feGaussianBlur stdDev=7 + feColorMatrix "1 0 0 0 0 / … / 0 0 0 20 -9" threshold from morph-showcase.vue:249-256). Each bridge plate tracks a piece's traveling position; while --split-t is low the plates' blurred alpha BLEEDS together → the threshold reads ONE merged metaball silhouette (the dock + its budding pieces are ONE goo body); as --split-t grows each plate's neck thins (the clip-path inset travel) until the blurred alpha no longer bridges the gap → the threshold splits them into separate silhouettes. The bridge plate's opacity ramps 1→0 over the LATE phase (t 0.55→1) so once the real pieces have detached, the decorative goo body fades and the clean real discs own the frame (the morph-bridge.css:121/146 opacity-crossover precedent). The bridge plates compose --glass-bg-floating (morph-bridge.css:72-77) so the goo reads as warm glass, not flat fill.

KEY INSIGHT: the goo necking IS the jubilance — it is the only thing that needs the SVG filter; the detached pieces are plain glass discs. So the expensive per-frame feGaussianBlur paint is confined to the SHORT necking window (t 0→0.55) and the SMALL bbox (dock + slots), not the whole transition.

== E. THE SAFARI-SAFE FILTER REGION (the budget) ==
filter:url(#…) IS cross-engine (WebKit supports SVG filter refs — the morph-bridge.css:6-12 "filter:url() IS cross-browser" verdict; this is NOT backdrop-filter:url() which Safari lacks). Three Safari/budget disciplines, all inherited from the shipped bridge: (1) the .dock-fission-bridge-goo container is a TIGHT box sized off the union bbox of {dock + all slots} (morph-bridge.css:50-61 — width/height off the spans + a 2.5rem pad), NOT inset:0 over the stage, so the per-frame feGaussianBlur repaints a small region; (2) `contain: layout paint` clips the filter work to it (line 59); (3) the SVG <filter> declares x/y/width/height region bounds ("-10% … 120%", morph-showcase.vue:244-247) so the filter sub-region is bounded — for an N-piece bbox this MUST be widened to cover the slot spread (the design pins it to the computed union-bbox-relative percentages, NOT the showcase's fixed 120%). PRM removes the bridge entirely (morph-bridge.css:154-158 + the spring's respectReducedMotion jump).

== F. COMPOSITOR-ONLY FLOOR (proof:no-layout-animation holds) ==
Every animated axis is f(--dock-split-t) or f(--stretch) (its derivative) — NEVER width/height/top/left. The pieces ride transform (translate+scale via ElementMorph OR a clip-path inset on a reserved footprint — the morph-bridge.css:89-98 "teardrop silhouette is the COMPOSITOR clip-path inset, NOT per-frame width/height" rule). The squish reads useLiquidFlex (--stretch capped at --dock-morph-max-stretch 1.08, useDockOrientationMorph.ts:97-105) so a piece SWELLS as it necks free and settles to fit (gap map "snap-recoil … ζ<1 overshoot", L335). will-change: clip-path, transform, opacity ONLY (morph-bridge.css:98).

== G. BIDIRECTIONAL RE-MERGE ==
Re-merge = the SAME spring run with target 0 (morphTo/toggle, useDockOrientationMorph.ts:209-217). The pieces fly back to the dock edge, the bridge plates' necks RE-FATTEN (clip inset shrinks), the blurred alpha re-bridges → the threshold re-fuses them into one body, the real pieces' opacity hands the frame back to the dock pill. The interruptible re-base (a re-merge interrupting a split) carries velocity (dockMorphContext.ts:255). Jubilance: the merged dock over-swells +8% then settles (useLiquidFlex --stretch on re-fusion, gap map L377 "Re-fusion squish overshoot").

== H. THE PRM=INSTANT SEAT ==
Mirror useDockOrientationMorph.pin() (lines 219-231): under prefers-reduced-motion the bridge never paints, no spring runs, the scalar + every piece's --split-t + the crossfade are written to the endpoint in ONE synchronous step, pieces snap to slots. The prefersReducedMotion() probe is the shipped matchMedia helper (useDockOrientationMorph.ts:158-164).

== THE WAVE SPEC: BE.W-DOCK-FISSION (critical) ==

== THE GATE: proof:dock-fission (device-free, ci) + the binding π ==
 F1 ONE-SPRING / SCALAR-BINDING: useDockFission owns exactly one SpringProgress; every piece position + neck is f(--dock-split-t) or f(--stretch) — NO second SpringProgress, NO free-running uTime/setTimeout/wall-clock (the morph-bridge.css:19-22 / morph-showcase M5 determinism clause; a frame at a given --dock-split-t is byte-reproducible).

 F3 REAL-DOM-vs-BRIDGE: the N pieces are real interactive DOM (z-10, tappable); the .dock-fission-bridge is decorative (z-0, pointer-events:none, aria-hidden — morph-bridge.css:33). The pieces are NOT crossfaded out (their opacity stays high); the bridge plates ARE (the late-phase opacity ramp).
 F4 SAFARI-SAFE FILTER REGION: the bridge uses filter:url(#…) (NOT backdrop-filter:url); the goo container is region-clipped (contain:layout paint + a union-bbox box, NOT inset:0); the SVG <filter> region bounds cover the slot spread; a self-test bite reds a backdrop-filter:url() re-introduction OR an inset:0 un-clipped goo container.

 F6 BIDIRECTIONAL + PRM: merge() runs the spring to 0 (re-fusion); pin(value) seats deterministically; a prefersReducedMotion() branch seats synchronously with NO bridge paint (the useDockOrientationMorph.pin precedent). + a 6-bite self-test (planted second-spring, planted wall-clock, planted backdrop-filter:url, planted layout-anim, planted missing-PRM-branch, planted un-clipped region).

THE STATE MACHINE — `BE.W-DOCK-CONTEXT-SILHOUETTE` (critical).

WHAT EXISTS (cited): `useDockState` (useDockState.ts:21,84) is a 3-state machine `collapsed|hover|pinned` — purely COLLAPSE state, never silhouette. The context seam is demo-private `useContextualDockLayers(route)` (demo/composables/useContextualDockLayers.ts:43) reading `route.meta.categoryId` → `CONTEXT_LAYER_MAP[id]` (demo/stories/dock-layer-contexts.ts:75), bound in BottomDock.vue:91-148 to `railItems`/`railContext` (→ `<DockStack>` fan rail) + `<DockSection :sections>` (display:contents grouping, DockSection.vue:91, box-INVIOLATE). So context today = facet-set swap + pane content, NOT silhouette. `proof:dock-contextual-layers` (proof-dock-contextual-layers.mjs:83) asserts exactly this: ONE route-keyed resolver, ≥3 contexts, rendered via group OR stack-rail, no hardcoded branch. The morph engine: `useDockMorphOrchestrator` (dockMorphContext.ts:143) owns ONE `SpringProgress` (DOCK_SPRING={response:0.32,ζ:0.7}, constants.ts:73) writing `--dock-morph-t` to root once/frame (dockMorphContext.ts:276); the box reserves `to` + composites `transform: scaleX(var(--dock-morph-scale))` (layers.css:73-87) — `--dock-morph-scale = max(reserve-floor, 1-(1-ratio)*t)`, ratio=`from/to` — so NO live-scalar layout read (CDP Layout flat). `useDockOrientationMorph.pin(value)` (useDockOrientationMorph.ts:219) is the deterministic exact-scalar capture seam (no spring). `morph-bridge.css` is the goo: two plates (`.dock-morph-bridge-plate--vertical/--horizontal`) each RESERVE max footprint + neck via `clip-path: inset(var(--neck) … round 999px)` interpolated on `--dock-morph-t`, opacity-crossfade at t≈0.5, `scale` reads `--stretch` (the useLiquidFlex derivative) — Safari-safe SVG-goo (`filter: url(#…)`), M5-deterministic (zero wall-clock).

THE DESIGN — declarative context→silhouette map. Mint a LIBRARY primitive `useDockContextSilhouette(options)` (`@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`) reading a `readonly DockSilhouetteDescriptor[]` (the descriptor lives in constants.ts beside DockSectionDescriptor — SFC-cannot-re-export-type home). Descriptor shape: `{ id, form: "bar"|"bar-pill"|"split"|"search", pieces?: DockPieceDescriptor[], anchorId? }`; a `DockPieceDescriptor` = `{ id, kind:"chip"|"pill"|"circle", glyph?, target:"left"|"center"|"right"|rect-fn, accent? }`. The active descriptor is resolved off a consumer-owned `:context` model (NOT route-hardcoded — the GENERAL-map discipline `proof:dock-contextual-layers` W1 already enforces; the demo binds it off `route.meta.categoryId` exactly as today, so the shell wiring is a thin re-point, not a re-author).
